pr.title: Revert "coverage: Enlarge empty spans during MIR instrumentation, not codegen"
pr.description:
Surprisingly, rust-lang/rust#144298 alone (extracted from rust-lang/rust#140847) was enough to re-trigger the failures observed in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/141577#issuecomment-3120667286.

---

This reverts commit f877aa7d14916f71a2f88c6d4c009e7ded7684c4.

pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Historical revert of a coverage change that moved empty-span enlargement out of LLVM codegen and into MIR InstrumentCoverage. Keeping empty coverage spans out of MIR instrumentation and enlarging them only in codegen's make_coords is the source-backed correct ordering; doing the enlargement earlier changed InstrumentCoverage and downstream CleanupPostBorrowck coverage statements and was enough to re-trigger the failures referenced by the PR. No compiler was built or executed here.
analysis.originalLogic: Restored behavior: MIR InstrumentCoverage leaves empty coverage spans empty through refinement, `remove_unwanted_overlapping_spans`, and deduplication/merging. Enlargement is done later in LLVM codegen: `make_coords` calls `let span = ensure_non_empty_span(source_map, span)?;`, and `ensure_non_empty_span` returns non-empty spans unchanged, otherwise tries to extend an empty span over an adjacent `{` or `}` by exactly one byte, returning `None` if neither is possible. Test expectations for InstrumentCoverage therefore retain empty-looking coverage regions such as `21:2: 21:2`, `29:2: 29:2`, `17:10: 17:10`, and `14:39: 14:39`; CleanupPostBorrowck shows the same empty spans downstream.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation moved `ensure_non_empty_span` into MIR InstrumentCoverage: after `discard_spans_overlapping_holes` and `remove_unwanted_overlapping_spans`, it retained and mutated covspans so empty spans became non-empty or were discarded, then deduplicated/merged them. In codegen, `make_coords` stopped enlarging empty spans and instead rejected them with `if span.is_empty() { debug_assert!(false, \"can't make coords from empty span: {span:?}\"); return None; }`. The revert removes that MIR enlargement/discard step, restores codegen enlargement, and reverts test expectations from enlarged ranges such as `21:1: 21:2` and `15:1: 15:2` back to empty ranges such as `21:2: 21:2` and `15:2: 15:2`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with coverage instrumentation whose MIR produces coverage spans where `span.lo() == span.hi()` (empty spans), especially synthetic/refined spans near line or column boundaries, match arms, async closures, and empty spans adjacent to `{` or `}`. Includes coverage MIR tests under `tests/mir-opt/coverage`, their `InstrumentCoverage` and `CleanupPostBorrowck` dumps, and coverage map tests under `tests/coverage`.
analysis.trigger: An empty coverage span reaches the InstrumentCoverage refinement pipeline. In the incorrect version, the early MIR enlargement rewrites it to cover an adjacent brace or drops it, changing emitted coverage spans before dedup/merge. In the correct version, the empty span remains empty through InstrumentCoverage and CleanupPostBorrowck and is handled only when codegen creates LLVM coverage coordinates.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and InstrumentCoverage extracts/refines coverage spans.
At least one refined coverage span is empty (`lo == hi`).
Correct path: codegen mapgen calls `make_coords`, which applies `ensure_non_empty_span` before computing coordinates.
Incorrect path: MIR InstrumentCoverage applies `ensure_non_empty_span` and `retain_mut` before `dedup_by`, while codegen rejects empty spans.
pitfalls: Do not assume empty coverage spans are invalid during MIR instrumentation; they are deliberately left empty until codegen coordinate generation.
Enlarging empty spans in InstrumentCoverage changes the observable MIR coverage statements and is not equivalent to enlarging them in codegen.
CleanupPostBorrowck does not perform this enlargement; its empty-span expectations are downstream of InstrumentCoverage and should move with it, not be 'fixed' independently to non-empty spans.
The codegen `debug_assert!(false, "can't make coords from empty span")` is specific to the reverted incorrect ordering; restoring `ensure_non_empty_span` in `make_coords` avoids that path.
Changing `BytePos` by 1 is only justified here after confirming the skipped byte is ASCII `{` or `}` at the appropriate adjacent position.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR coverage tests: compare `InstrumentCoverage` dumps for `branch_match_arms`, `instrument_coverage`, and `instrument_coverage_cleanup`, asserting empty regions remain empty (e.g. `21:2: 21:2`, `29:2: 29:2`, `17:10: 17:10`, `14:39: 14:39`) rather than being widened to the previous column/brace. Check `instrument_coverage_cleanup.main.CleanupPostBorrowck.diff` to ensure CleanupPostBorrowck preserves the same empty spans from InstrumentCoverage. Cover async closures with `tests/coverage/async_closure.cov-map`, where the corrected mapping splits `11:34` to `11:35` and `11:35` to `11:36` versus the incorrect single widened mapping. Add a differential test toggling only the location of `ensure_non_empty_span`: early MIR enlargement/discard versus late codegen enlargement, holding the program and InstrumentCoverage span extraction fixed. No execution or compiler build is claimed by this knowledge.
